backtest.methodology: Long-only spot. Next-bar-open fills; fees + slippage charged on every fill, including stop exits (gap-aware: a gap below the stop fills at the open, not the stop price). BTC daily SMA(200) regime filter gates all entries for both strategies. ATR-chandelier trailing stop. Bootstrap 95% confidence interval on average R. Time-shift placebo: 200 simulations with the real signals circular-shifted to random dates, same prices and costs — reports what percentile the real result ranks at among the shuffled copies. Fixed 70/30 in-sample/out-of-sample split by date (not tuned to the split). strategies.py and engine.py (the strategy and backtest-engine code) were used exactly as supplied, unmodified, with no parameter tuned to produce these numbers.
backtest.verdict: No strategy passed every required gate on either dataset. Neither trend_ensemble nor tsmom is a candidate for paper trading as-is — see the gates table for each strategy below for exactly which check(s) failed.

datasets.label: Coinbase Exchange (Data B)
datasets.source: Coinbase Exchange, via ccxt (coinbaseexchange) — Kraken's own downloadable history and Binance (geo-blocked) were tried first and were not usable; see data_sources.md on the source branch
datasets.note: Long multi-year history; each coin starts at its own real Coinbase listing date (2015-2025 depending on coin — BNB only has ~1yr, for example)

trend_ensemble.label: Donchian Breakout Ensemble
trend_ensemble.description: Votes across multiple Donchian-channel breakout lookbacks; enters when enough of them agree, sized/trailed with ATR.

tsmom.label: Time-Series Momentum
tsmom.description: Enters in the direction of each symbol's own recent trailing return, sized/trailed with ATR.

candidates_schema.tested_at: ISO8601 UTC timestamp of when this candidate was backtested
candidates_schema.name: short human-readable name
candidates_schema.description: what this candidate actually is -- a parameter variant of the live strategy, or a genuinely new strategy idea, and why it was tried
candidates_schema.based_on: live_strategy, or null for a from-scratch new strategy
candidates_schema.dataset: kraken_720 | long -- which strategy_pack_run dataset this run used
candidates_schema.cost_preset: which strategy_pack_run/engine.py COST_PRESETS entry was used (kraken_T3_taker is standard for gating)
candidates_schema.avg_r_ci: [low, high] 95% bootstrap CI on avg R
candidates_schema.gates: same 5-key PASS/FAIL dict as strategies.*.gates.<dataset>, plus overall
candidates_schema.notes: free text -- caveats, what was tried, why it did or did not work
candidates_schema.config_key: REQUIRED for kind=parameter_variant: dotted path into config/config.yaml this candidate changes, e.g. 'trade_planner.stop_atr_mult'. null for kind=new_strategy (no mechanical promotion path exists for a from-scratch strategy -- it needs a human to wire it into src/ by hand).
candidates_schema.config_value: REQUIRED for kind=parameter_variant: the exact new value tested, same type as the live config key (e.g. 1.8). This is the value the auto-promotion step writes verbatim if the candidate passes -- it must be the literal tested value, not an approximation.
candidates_schema.promoted_at: null until auto-promoted; ISO8601 UTC timestamp set by the Routine's promotion phase the day it applied this candidate's config_key/config_value to config/config.yaml. Once set, this candidate is never promoted again (idempotency guard).
candidates_schema.promoted_pr_url: null until promoted_at is set; the GitHub PR URL that made the config.yaml change.

candidates.name: trade_planner.min_risk_reward = 2.44
candidates.description: Parameter variant of the live strategy: raise the planner's take-profit R:R target from 2.0 to 2.44 (hyperopt-chosen). Wider targets win less often but bigger.
candidates.notes: Chosen by strategy_pack_run/hyperopt_param.optimize_live_bot_param (15 calls, bounds 1.5-3.0, train-split avg R objective on the long dataset; best 2.435 rounded to 2.44, train avg R 0.805 vs ~0.59 at 2.0). Gated with fresh 200-sim placebo, 70/30 split, kraken_T3_taker. Long set: PASS 5/5. Baseline 2.0 same run: 562 trades, avg R 0.52 CI [0.36,0.68], return 387%, maxDD -29.2%, Sharpe 1.00 (5/5). 2.44 improves avg R/return/Sharpe but deepens maxDD (-29.2% -> -32.8%) and cuts win rate 48%->43%.

candidates.name: trade_planner.min_risk_reward = 2.44
candidates.description: Parameter variant of the live strategy: raise the planner's take-profit R:R target from 2.0 to 2.44 (hyperopt-chosen). Wider targets win less often but bigger.
candidates.notes: Chosen by strategy_pack_run/hyperopt_param.optimize_live_bot_param (15 calls, bounds 1.5-3.0, train-split avg R objective on the long dataset; best 2.435 rounded to 2.44, train avg R 0.805 vs ~0.59 at 2.0). Gated with fresh 200-sim placebo, 70/30 split, kraken_T3_taker. 2-year set: FAIL (3/5): avg R CI low <0 and placebo 90th-pct gate missed (return 90th, avg R 83.5th pct). Baseline 2.0 same run: 154 trades, avg R 0.18 (CI low -0.08), return 22.5%, Sharpe 0.68, 4/5. 2.44 is worse than baseline here on every metric. Not eligible for promotion (needs PASS on both datasets); likely train-split overfit on the long set.

candidates.name: trade_planner.trend_stop_atr_bonus = 0.47
candidates.description: Parameter variant of the live strategy: widen the extra stop (ATR multiples) applied when ADX confirms a trend from 0.3 to 0.47 (hyperopt-chosen).
candidates.notes: Chosen by hyperopt_param.optimize_live_bot_param (15 calls, bounds 0.0-1.0, train-split avg R objective on the long set; best 0.466 rounded to 0.47). The objective surface was flat/noisy (train avg R ~0.60-0.74 across the range; live 0.3 ~0.66), so this is a weak signal. Gated with fresh 200-sim placebo, 70/30 split. Long set: PASS 5/5. Baseline 0.3: 562 trades, avg R 0.52 [0.36,0.68], return 387%, Sharpe 1.00, maxDD -29.2%. 0.47: avg R 0.55, return 387%, Sharpe 1.00, maxDD -29.6% -- essentially a tie, small avg R gain only.
